summary: This refresh needs to be honest: Silence Therapeutics has already run hard ahead of its own catalyst, and real upside has compressed well below this board's 200%+ bar. The stock has roughly doubled since this name was first picked two weeks ago (from ~$6-7 to $11.50), and the 7-analyst consensus of $29.17 now implies only +154% from here — real and broad, but no longer a clean moonshot on a strict basis. What hasn't changed: the SANRECO Phase 2 topline data for divesiran in polycythemia vera is genuinely due in August 2026, and this remains a real binary readout. The market has simply already priced in a meaningful chunk of the optimism ahead of the actual data.

catalysts.description: Topline data for the Phase 2 SANRECO study of divesiran 6mg in phlebotomy-dependent polycythemia vera patients, due August 2026 — a real, near-term binary readout that the stock has been running up into.

risks: Real upside has compressed to +154% (7-analyst consensus) — the stock has already run hard (roughly doubled over two weeks) ahead of the actual data, meaning much of the optimism may already be priced in
This remains a genuinely binary Phase 2 readout — a disappointing result would likely reverse a meaningful chunk of the recent run-up
Near the 52-week high heading into the catalyst — less margin for error than when this name was trading near its lows
H.C. Wainwright's $75 target is a real outlier well above the broader consensus — treating it as the base case would be a mistake
Small-cap biotech volatility cuts both ways — the same mechanics driving the recent run-up can reverse sharply on any pre-data sentiment shift
